Chronology 4 — Abraham

The Bible's text

  • Gen 12–25: the call, the covenant, circumcision. Ishmael (by Hagar) is blessed and made a great nation, but the covenant runs through Isaac (by Sarah): "My covenant I will establish with Isaac" (Gen 17:19–21).
  • The binding (Gen 22): the son to be offered is named explicitly — Isaac.

The Qur'an's text

  • Ibrahim shatters the idols and argues against his people (Q 21:51–70; 6:74–79).
  • *The sacrificed son is unnamed** in the sacrifice passage: a "forbearing boy" (ghulam halim), the dream, the submission, the ransom (Q 37:99–113). The text does not state Isaac or* Ishmael at the moment of the offering.
  • Classical Muslim consensus → Ishmael, but early exegetes were divided (several major early authorities said Isaac); the Ishmael identification is largely post-Qur'anic tafsir, not the Qur'anic wording itself.
  • Ibrahim and Ismail raise the foundations of the Kaaba (Q 2:127); Ibrahim is a hanif, "neither Jew nor Christian" but a muslim (submitter) (Q 3:67).

Collision

  1. Who was offered? The Bible is explicit (Isaac). The Qur'an is silent; the Ishmael answer is tradition filling a textual gap. By the dossier's own rule (Methodology §1: text > tradition), this is a case where one side's confident claim is exegetical, not scriptural — and that must be stated honestly against the Muslim popular claim, just as the Bible's spurious Trinity proof-text was stated against the Christian one.
  2. Covenant line: Bible → Isaac/Israel; Qur'an → Ibrahim as the proto-muslim and the Kaaba/Hajj origin (no biblical parallel).
  3. "Abraham was a muslim" (Q 3:67) vs. Abraham as father of Israel and of faith (Gen; Rom 4).

Arbiter verdict — Abraham

Present. Shared patriarch and monotheistic exemplar. Bible: explicit Isaac, covenant through Isaac. Qur'an: unnamed son, Ibrahim as universal hanif, Kaaba foundation.

Weigh.

  • Textual explicitness: the Bible names the son; the Qur'an does not. The famous "it was Ishmael" is tradition, and saying so is required by symmetry — the same scalpel used on the Comma Johanneum.
  • Unattested historical claims: the Kaaba's Abrahamic construction and "Abraham was a muslim" have no pre-Islamic documentary or biblical corroboration; they are faith claims, not history (Methodology §1).
  • Not a corruption proof either way: differing emphases here do not, by themselves, prove tampering of either text.

Judge. On "which text actually says who was offered?": the Bible wins on explicitness; the Muslim Ishmael claim is, strictly, extra-Qur'anic. On the theological repurposing (proto-muslim, Kaaba): these are unfalsifiable faith claims with no external support — the arbiter records them as claims, not data, and rules neither true nor false (out of remit). Net: a point to textual precision on the Bible's side, and a flag that popular Muslim apologetics here repeats exactly the tradition-as-text error the dossier charged against Christian apologetics.
